Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

What we integrate with

Examples of systems commonly found in real estate. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

  • Real estate CRM and pre-sales

    Source of truth for leads, visits, partners and bookings. We read and write through its APIs, webhooks or approved exports and keep one record per buyer, with every source preserved for attribution.

    • Sell.Do
    • LeadSquared
    • Salesforce
    • Zoho CRM

  • Property portals and ad lead sources

    Where most enquiries start. Portal lead delivery is push or pull depending on the package and is set up through each portal's account manager; we log every payload so a dropped lead can be traced.

    • 99acres
    • MagicBricks
    • Housing.com
    • Meta and Google lead forms

  • Real estate ERP and accounting

    Holds inventory, price lists, payment plans, demands, receipts and brokerage payables. Demand letters and payouts are generated from its data, through an API or approved export, and posted back only after approval.

    • Farvision
    • SAP
    • Tally

  • Project controls and site apps

    Schedules, BOQs, daily reports and material records for contractors and developer project teams, and the baseline against which reported progress is compared.

    • Primavera P6
    • Microsoft Project
    • Powerplay
    • Procore

  • Leasing and co-working platforms

    Leases, memberships, inventory, billing and access for commercial landlords and operators, and the source for lease calendars and occupancy.

    • Yardi
    • MRI Software
    • Nexudus
    • OfficeRnD

  • Government and regulator portals

    Where project updates, agreements, reports and notices are filed. Our workflows prepare drafts, evidence and reminders; filing stays with the responsible person.

    • State RERA portals
    • State registration and stamp duty portals
    • FIU-IND FINGate
    • Shram Suvidha and state labor portals

  • Messaging and telephony

    Buyer and tenant channels with their own rules: opt-in and approved templates for WhatsApp, registered headers and templates for SMS, a seven-day limit on enquiry-based calls and SMS, and preference checks for promotional calls.

    • WhatsApp Business Platform via a provider
    • DLT-registered SMS gateway
    • Cloud telephony with 140-series numbers

The measures we propose to track

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Speed to first contact
Median time from lead creation in any source to the first meaningful contact by automation or an executive, by source and for staffed and unstaffed hours.Why it matters: Portal and ad leads compare several projects at once, and the first useful reply often wins the site visit.
Lead-to-site-visit conversion
Share of qualified leads in a period that complete a site or video visit, by project, source, partner and executive.Why it matters: Shows whether response, qualification and visit booking work together, and which sources deserve more spend.
Visit-to-booking conversion
Share of completed visits that lead to a booking within an agreed window, from CRM records.Why it matters: Measures the quality of visits and follow-up, not just their number.
Partner registration conflict rate
Share of channel partner registrations flagged as duplicates or conflicts, with the median time to a recorded decision.Why it matters: Few conflicts and quick decisions protect partner trust and keep brokerage moving.
Booking-to-agreement registration time
Median days from booking to a registered agreement for sale, split into buyer document time, internal verification time and registration scheduling.Why it matters: Separates delays the developer can fix from buyer and registration delays, and keeps advances within the RERA limit for longer files.
Demand-to-collection days
Median days from demand letter release to receipt of the full amount, by tower, milestone and loan-funded or self-funded buyers.Why it matters: The cash flow measure that milestone evidence, lender packs and reminders are meant to improve.
Snag closure time
Median time from a snag being logged to verified closure, with the share reopened by the buyer or tenant.Why it matters: Drives handover satisfaction and shows which contractors or trades need attention.
Daily report timeliness
Share of site days with a complete daily report submitted before the agreed cut-off, by site and engineer.Why it matters: Late or missing reports hide slippage, idle labor and material risks until they are expensive.
Renewals decided before notice deadline
Share of leases and memberships reaching a recorded renewal or exit decision before the notice or lock-in date.Why it matters: Late decisions turn into vacancy or rushed concessions.
Safety incident acknowledgement time
Time from an incident or near-miss report to acknowledgement by the site safety officer, with the share of corrective actions closed by their due date.Why it matters: Shows whether reports reach the accountable person quickly and lead to action.

How we connect systems responsibly

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
